content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides D4 vs C2 as UNDERDETERMINED from Luke 2:48-49's 'thy father' versus 'my Father's business,' so it invokes the rule on single verses carrying two senses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.' Reading A: the Luke 2:48-49 two-sense phrasing cannot support UNDERDETERMINED; both senses stand. Reading B: one sense may be qualified by the other, leaving the point underdetermined.","why":"The judge marks the Luke 2:48-49 point UNDERDETERMINED even though its 'thy father' and 'my Father's business' are treated as two senses in one verse, which K-S2 says are not open and both stand."}
